### sequential-implies-continuous-at  *(trust: well-known)*

*trusted code: `ineq`, `arith`, `crs`* -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

- `nn-recip-succ-pos` -- *warrant informal:* 1/(n+1) is a positive real for every natural n.  Rigorous from the axioms
   present, hence `informal' rather than `well-known': n + 1 >= 1 > 0 in RR
   (nn-in-rr and the order axioms), recip of a nonzero real is real
   (rr-recip-closed), and it is positive because a positive reciprocal is
   forced by a * recip a = 1 (rr-recip-inverse) together with
   rr-leq-mul-nonneg.  Not mechanised: it needs recip-order lemmas the tree
   does not have yet.
- `nn-recip-succ-small` -- *warrant informal:* For every eps > 0 there is a natural n with 1/(n+1) < eps.  The corollary of
   nn-unbounded-in-rr that eps-arguments actually consume: apply unboundedness
   to x = 1/eps to get n > 1/eps, hence n + 1 > 1/eps > 0, hence
   1/(n+1) < eps by antitonicity of recip on the positives.  A rigorous paper
   proof exists from nn-unbounded-in-rr plus the ordered-field axioms, hence
   `informal'; mechanising it needs the recip-monotonicity lemmas (0 < a =>
   0 < recip a; 0 < a < b => recip b < recip a), which the tree does not have.
   Adding those two and proving this would trade one assertion for two, so it
   was deliberately not done -- see the note in separable.scm.
- `metric-dist-real` -- *warrant well-known:* The distance is real-valued: DIST(s) maps PTS(s) x PTS(s) into RR, so d(s)(x,y) in RR.  Codomain typing of the metric op (the op-clause in the METRIC-SPACE declaration).

### smith-diagonalization  *(trust: well-known)*

*trusted code: `arith`, `crs`* -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

- `identmat-left-identity` -- *warrant proof:* I_m P = P: the (i,c) entry is sum_j delta_ij P_jc, whose only surviving term
   (j=i) is 1*P_ic = P_ic (matmul-entry + entry-of-identmat + finsum-single-
   support + ring-mul-left-id).  Proof structure worked out in identmat-build.scm.
- `identmat-right-identity` -- *warrant proof:* P I_n = P, the right-handed mirror of identmat-left-identity (only the c=j
   term of sum_j P_ij delta_jc survives).
- `identmat-type` -- *warrant reference:* IDENTMAT(A,n) is an n-by-n matrix over CARR A (its entries are ONE/ZERO of A).
- `nn-not-le-zero-pos` -- *warrant well-known:* 1 <= j => not(j <= 0) for j in NN (0 is least, and j >= 1 > 0).
- `nn-pos-is-succ` -- *warrant well-known:* a positive nat is a successor (n>=1 => n = succ(n-1), n-1 in NN).
- `one-in-interval` -- *warrant well-known:* 1 in [1, succ n] (1 <= 1 <= succ n).
- `entry-in-carrier` -- *warrant well-known:* The (i,j) entry of an m-by-n matrix over X lies in X.
- `gauge-is-degree` -- *warrant proof:* GAUGE(s) = CHOICE(EUCLIDEAN-GAUGES s) is in FUN(CARR s, NN) and has division-
   with-remainder: IS-EUCLIDEAN-RING(s) makes EUCLIDEAN-GAUGES(s) inhabited
   (euclidean-ring-has-gauge + gauges-mem-build), so the epsilon pick lands in
   it (choice-axiom) and the SEP slices give both conjuncts.  MACHINE-PROVEN in
   archive/calculus-pre-rename/gauge-proof.scm.
- `elem-f-type` -- *warrant reference:* ELEM-F(A,n,k,l) is an n-by-n matrix over CARR A (its entries are ONE/ZERO of A;
   matof-in-mat on the swap entry function).
- `matmul-type` -- *warrant reference:* MAT(m,n,CARR A) x MAT(n,k,CARR A) -> MAT(m,k,CARR A): the tabulated product
   is a matrix whose entries are FINSUMs in the carrier (matof-in-mat +
   finsum-type).
- `matmul-entry` -- *warrant reference:* (P Q)_{ic} = sum_{j=1}^{n} P_{ij}*Q_{jc}, the product summed in A's additive
   group over j in 1..n (entry-of-matof on the MATMUL tabulation).
- `interval-card-in-nn` -- *warrant well-known:* INTERVAL(a,b) with b in NN is finite, so its cardinality is a natural number.
- `matprod-summand-type` -- *warrant well-known:* j |-> P_{ij}.Q_{jc} is a function [1,n] -> CARR A for P:MAT(m,n), Q:MAT(n,nn)
   (entry-in-carrier gives both factors in CARR A; MUL closes; CARR(RAG)=CARR A).
- `elem-f-ck-off` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{jc} = 0 for c=k, j/=l.
- `ring-mul-zero-right` -- *warrant well-known:* a.0 = 0: symmetric to ring-mul-zero-left.  Lang, Algebra II.1.
- `ras-id` -- *warrant proof:* identity of a ring's additive group is the ring's zero.
- `finsum-single-support` -- *warrant well-known:* If f(j)=0 for every j in the finite S except j=i0, then FINSUM(ag,f,S)=f(i0).
- `elem-f-ck-at` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{lc} = 1 for c=k.
- `elem-f-cl-off` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{jc} = 0 for c=l, j/=k.
- `elem-f-cl-at` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{kc} = 1 for c=l.
- `elem-f-co-off` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{jc} = 0 for c/=k, c/=l, j/=c.
- `elem-f-co-at` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{cc} = 1 for c/=k, c/=l.
- `entry-of-identmat` -- *warrant reference:* (IDENTMAT A n)_{ij} = 1 if i=j else 0 (entry-of-matof on the Kronecker delta).
- `elem-f-col-k` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{ik} = 1 if i=l else 0 (k/=l).
- `elem-f-col-l` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{il} = 1 if i=k else 0 (k/=l).
- `elem-f-col-other` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{ic} = 1 if i=c else 0 (c/=k, c/=l).
- `matrix-entry-extensionality` -- *warrant well-known:* Two m-by-n matrices over X with equal entries are equal (tuple/list
   extensionality applied row- and entry-wise).
- `elem-f-rk-off` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{ij} = 0 for i=k, j/=l.
- `ring-mul-zero-left` -- *warrant well-known:* 0.a = 0: a.0 = a.(0+0) = a.0 + a.0, cancel a.0 in the additive group.  Lang, Algebra II.1.
- `elem-f-rk-at` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{il} = 1 for i=k.
- `elem-f-rl-off` -- *warrant reference:* F[k,l]_{ij} = 0 for i=l, j/=k.

   k) is again a function NN -> PTS(s).  Pure composition typing.
- `strictly-mono-ge-id` -- *warrant proof:* NN-induction on k.  k=0: 0 <= phi(0) (NN is nonnegative).  k -> succ k:
   phi(k) >= k (IH) and phi(succ k) > phi(k) (strict monotonicity at k < succ k),
   so phi(succ k) > k, i.e. phi(succ k) >= succ k on NN.  Standard.

### subsequence-principle  *(trust: well-known)*

proven modulo:

- `nn-finite-subset-bounded` -- *warrant well-known:* A finite subset T of NN is bounded.  By finite-set-induction (cardinality.scm,
   primitive) on T: the empty set is bounded by N = 0, and if T is bounded by N
   then T u {x} is bounded by max(succ x, N) (nn-pair-upper-bound, order-lemmas).
   Hence some N in NN has y < N for every y in T, so no y >= N is in T.  The
   contrapositive of `inf-subset-nn-unbounded' (diagonalization-lemmas.scm),
   which asserts the same equivalence from the other side and is warranted the
   same way.  Not mechanised: the induction runs over a COMP class
   { T | T subset NN => bounded } and wants the comprehension-membership
   bookkeeping, sethood of T, and the max-of-two-naturals brick threaded through
   -- routine, and no library payoff beyond this one citation.
- `subsequence-capture` -- *warrant informal:* Every infinite set of naturals carries a strictly increasing enumeration.
   Take f = nn-enum(s); nn-enum-spec gives exactly that f is in fun(NN, s) and
   strictly order-preserving.  subsequence-capture is the existential shadow
   of nn-enum-spec.

   nxt(k,u) is the successor SET, supplied as a VNB-LAMBDA, so callers avoid
   the (LIST k u y)-in-R comprehension/sethood/NTH plumbing (O1 of
   archive/calculus-pre-rename/block-family-rederive.scm).  Accepted asserted during library-build.
- `fun-codomain-superset` -- *warrant well-known:* A function into B is a function into any superset C (fun-codomain-iff + subset-mem).
- `submodule-subset` -- *warrant reference:* A submodule is by definition a subset of the vectors.
- `proper-subset-witness` -- *warrant well-known:* If a subset b but a != b then by extensionality some x in b is not in a.
- `dual-norm-on-nonneg` -- *warrant reference:* DUAL-NORM-ON is defined by IOTA over c in RR with 0<=c, so for a bounded
   functional it is a nonnegative real.
- `hb-gap` -- *warrant reference:* Hahn-Banach gap (real, one dimension): with M = ||f||_s, for z,w in s
   f(w-z) <= M||w-z|| <= M(||z+v||+||w+v||), so sup_z(-f(z)-M||z+v||) <=
   inf_w(-f(w)+M||w+v||); RR order-completeness gives a separating alpha, whence
   |f(y)+r.alpha| <= M||y+r.v|| for all y in s, r in RR.
- `hb-extend-construct` -- *warrant reference:* Extending a linear functional one dimension: with v notin s every element of
   s + RR.v is uniquely y + r.v, so g(y+r.v) = f(y) + r.alpha is a well-defined
   linear functional on s + RR.v extending f, for any scalar alpha.  Standard
   linear algebra; alpha is fixed only by the bound (hb-gap).
- `span-add-one-membership` -- *warrant proof:* Separation membership: SPAN-ADD-ONE(m,s,v) = SEP(w in VEC(m) | exists y in s,
   r in RR. w = y + r.v); a member iff in VEC(m) and it so decomposes.
- `span-add-one-submodule` -- *warrant reference:* t + RR.v is closed under addition, negation and the scalar action and
   contains 0, so it is a submodule.
- `span-add-one-superset` -- *warrant reference:* Every y in t equals y + 0.v, so t is contained in t + RR.v.
- `extends-on-trans` -- *warrant reference:* If g2=g1 on t, g1=f on s, and s subset t, then g2=f on s.
- `vnrm-real` -- *warrant reference:* VNRM(m) : VEC(m) -> RR, so the norm of a vector is a real.
- `vnrm-nonneg` -- *warrant reference:* Norm nonnegativity, a defining law of IS-NORMED-VECTOR-SPACE.
- `linfun-app-abs-real` -- *warrant reference:* A linear functional on t maps into RR, so |g(w)| is a real for w in t.
- `dual-norm-on-le-bound` -- *warrant reference:* DUAL-NORM-ON(m,s,g) is the least c>=0 bounding |g(w)| by c*||w|| on s
   (IOTA least-upper-bound), hence <= any such bound c.
- `le-bound-mono` -- *warrant well-known:* Reals: from p<=a*n, a<=b and 0<=n, scale a<=b by n>=0 to a*n<=b*n, then
   transitivity gives p<=b*n.
- `span-add-one-has-v` -- *warrant reference:* v = 0 + 1.v with 0 in t, so v is in t + RR.v.
- `vec-is-set` -- *warrant reference:* VEC(m) in SET, a defining clause of IS-NORMED-VECTOR-SPACE (definedness).
- `linfun-on-vec-is-linfun` -- *warrant reference:* IS-LINEAR-FUNCTIONAL-ON m (VEC m) f and IS-LINEAR-FUNCTIONAL m f unfold to the
   same conjunction (f in FUN(VEC m,RR), additive, homogeneous over VEC m).
- `dual-norm-le-bound` -- *warrant reference:* DUAL-NORM(m,f) is the least c>=0 bounding |f(w)| by c*||w|| on VEC(m) (IOTA
   least-upper-bound), hence <= any such bound c.
- `dual-norm-nonneg` -- *warrant reference:* DUAL-NORM is defined by IOTA over c in RR with 0<=c, so for a bounded f it is
   a nonnegative real.
- `line-has-v` -- *warrant reference:* v = 1.v, so v is in RR.v = LINE(m,v).
- `gof-in-fun` -- *warrant reference:* g : VEC(m) -> RR (bounded linear functional) composed with f : RR -> VEC(m)
   is g o f : RR -> RR.
- `gof-taylor-diff` -- *warrant reference:* A bounded linear functional g is linear and continuous, so it commutes with the
   Caratheodory derivative: if f^(k) is norm-continuous / vector-differentiable
   with factor phi, then (g o f)^(k) = g o f^(k) is continuous / differentiable
   with factor g o phi.  Hence g o f is scalar-Taylor-differentiable to order n.
- `taylor-g-in-fun` -- *warrant reference:* G(t)=f(x)-TAYLOR-POLY(f,t,n,x) maps RR to RR (finite sum of products of
   reals), for each degree n in NN.
- `taylor-h-in-fun` -- *warrant reference:* H(t)=(x-t)^(n+1) maps RR to RR, for each degree n in NN.
- `taylor-gmvt-cont` -- *warrant reference:* G and H are continuous on [a,x]: H is a polynomial, G a finite sum of products
   of the continuous derivatives f^(k) with polynomials (taylor-G-cont/H-cont).
- `taylor-gmvt-diff` -- *warrant reference:* G and H are differentiable at every real point of (a,x) (taylor-G-diff/H-diff
   give the explicit derivatives), so each has SOME derivative there.
- `binneg-in-fun-rr` -- *warrant well-known:* Closure of a primitive numeric domain under its arithmetic operation; standard.
- `binplus-in-fun-rr` -- *warrant well-known:* Closure of a primitive numeric domain under its arithmetic operation; standard.
- `bintimes-in-fun-rr` -- *warrant well-known:* Closure of a primitive numeric domain under its arithmetic operation; standard.
- `gmvt-aux-cont` -- *warrant reference:* h = (g(b)-g(a))f - (f(b)-f(a))g is a linear combination of f and g, hence
   continuous wherever both f and g are (calculus.pdf Thm 2.11).
- `gmvt-aux-diff` -- *warrant reference:* h'(x) = (g(b)-g(a))f'(x) - (f(b)-f(a))g'(x), from deriv-sum/scalar-mult on the
   linear combination h = (g(b)-g(a))f - (f(b)-f(a))g (calculus.pdf Thm 2.11).
- `max-val-strict-interior` -- *warrant well-known:* c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(a)<h(c) => a<c<b (a strict max above equal endpoints is interior).
- `rr-prod-nonpos-pos` -- *warrant well-known:* u*v<=0 with v>0 forces u<=0.
- `rr-prod-nonpos-neg` -- *warrant well-known:* u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.
- `continuous-nonpos-right` -- *warrant well-known:* A function continuous at th that is <=0 on a right-neighborhood (th,bb) is
   <=0 at th (sign preservation under continuity / one-sided limit).
- `continuous-nonneg-left` -- *warrant well-known:* A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is
   >=0 at th.
- `min-val-strict-interior` -- *warrant well-known:* c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.
- `deriv-neg` -- *warrant reference:* Derivative of -f is -f': f(x)-f(a)=phi(x)(x-a) gives (-f)(x)-(-f)(a) =
   (-phi)(x)(x-a), with -phi continuous at a and value -L.
- `rr-midpoint-between` -- *warrant well-known:* a<b => exists m with a<m<b.
- `diff-value-real` -- *warrant informal:* IS-DIFF-AT's definition includes (IN L RR) as a conjunct.
- `cont-agree-off-pt` -- *warrant well-known:* fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt).  pt is
   a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit
   of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
- `taylor-g-diff` -- *warrant reference:* Telescoping: d/dt[f(x)-Sum_{k<=n} f^(k)(t)(x-t)^k/k!] = -(f^(n+1)(t)/n!)(x-t)^n.
   Differentiate term k by the product rule: the f^(k+1)(t)(x-t)^k/k! piece of
   term k cancels the -f^(k+1)(t)(x-t)^k/k! piece of term k+1, leaving only the
   last -(f^(n+1)(t)/n!)(x-t)^n.  Standard (calculus.pdf Taylor section).
- `taylor-h-diff` -- *warrant reference:* d/dt[(x-t)^(n+1)] = -(n+1)(x-t)^n (chain rule on the polynomial).
- `taylor-g-at-x` -- *warrant reference:* G(x) = f(x) - TAYLOR-POLY(f,x,n,x) = f(x) - f(x) = 0 (taylor-poly-at-center).
- `taylor-g-at-a` -- *warrant reference:* G(a) = f(x) - TAYLOR-POLY(f,a,n,x) (beta).
- `taylor-h-at-x` -- *warrant reference:* H(x) = (x-x)^(n+1) = 0^(n+1) = 0.
- `taylor-h-at-a` -- *warrant reference:* H(a) = (x-a)^(n+1) (beta).
- `rr-power-pos` -- *warrant well-known:* 0<d gives 0<d^n for every n (induction: d^0=1>0; d^(n+1)=d*d^n, product of
   positives).
- `taylor-deriv-real` -- *warrant reference:* f^(n+1)(t) is the derivative value of the differentiable f^(n) at t, hence
   real (IS-DIFF-AT carries its value in RR).
- `taylor-poly-in-rr` -- *warrant reference:* TAYLOR-POLY is a finite sum of products of reals, hence real.
- `taylor-clear` -- *warrant well-known:* Substitute gx=hx=0, ha=d, ga=r: (-(fn1/n!)pw)(-d) = (-(n+1)pw)(-r), i.e.
   (fn1/n!)pw*d = (n+1)pw*r; cancel pw/=0 and multiply by n! (using
   (n+1)*n! = (n+1)!) to get (n+1)! r = fn1 d.  Pure real arithmetic.
- `g-of-remainder` -- *warrant reference:* g linear: g(f(x) (-) p) = g(f(x)) - g(p) = (g o f)(x) - g(TAYLOR-POLY-V).  g
   commutes with the finite VADD/ACT sum and with f^(k)(a), so
   g(TAYLOR-POLY-V(f,a,x,n)) = Sum ((x-a)^k/k!) g(f^(k)(a))
   = Sum ((x-a)^k/k!) (g o f)^(k)(a) = TAYLOR-POLY(g o f, a, n, x).
- `gof-nth-deriv` -- *warrant reference:* By induction on k using commutation 1's factor identity, (g o f)^(k) = g o f^(k)
   as functions; evaluating the (n+1)-st at t gives (g o f)^(n+1)(t) = g(f^(n+1)(t)).
- `nth-deriv-v-in-vec` -- *warrant reference:* Each vector derivative f^(k) maps RR into VEC(m) (IS-DIFF-AT-V pins the value
   in VEC(m)); so f^(k)(t) is a vector.
- `blf-app-real` -- *warrant reference:* A bounded linear functional g maps VEC(m) into RR, so g(v) is a real.
- `dual-norm-is-bound` -- *warrant reference:* The operator norm DUAL-NORM(m,f) satisfies |f(x)| <= ||f|| ||x|| for every x
   (it is defined as the least such bound; in particular it IS a bound).
- `bdd-linfun-abs-real` -- *warrant reference:* A bounded linear functional maps VEC(m) into RR, so |f(x)| is a real.
- `rr-mul-le-right` -- *warrant well-known:* a<=b and 0<=c give a*c <= b*c.
